newsitem.title: USA: Semiconductor stocks ride Intel coattails.
newsitem.headline: Semiconductor stocks ride Intel coattails.

text.p: Stocks of several computer chipmakers surged on Thursday amid optimism that record demand for Intel Corp.'s Pentium microprocessors will boost sales of other types of chips.

An Intel executive told Wall Street on Wednesday that his company's factories cannot keep up with orders from personal computer makers. That means PC companies are placing big orders for other types of chips as well, analysts said.
"The boom days for the chip companies may not be here yet, but the bad days for are certainly over," said David Wu, an analyst at Chicago Corp in New York.
Shares of Micron Technology Inc, one of the biggest makers of memory chips, rose 1 to 37 on New York Stock Exchange trading of 7.45 million shares, making it the most active stock on the Big Board.
Shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc, a microprocessor maker that competes against Intel, rose 58 to 27-1/2 in early afternoon trading.
"If Intel is sold out, it doesn't take a genius to guess that AMD is going to get some of the scraps," Wu said.
LSI Logic Corp, a maker of consumer electronic chips, was up 3/8 at 31-1/4.

On Monday, the semiconductor industry's chief trade association said orders have risen to the highest level in more than a year, indicating that semiconductor companies are recovering from a glut of chips.
Analysts said strong demand for PCs from corporate buyers and more stable prices of memory chips should put the industry back on track to grow at about 20 percent in 1997.
The Philadelphia semiconductor index, which measures the performance of several key chip stocks, rose 4.34 points, or 1.7 percent, to 255.41, following Intel's gains Thursday.
